citations.quote:
The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K:S^1\hookrightarrow S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot in the standard oriented three-sphere, and let $F\subset S^3$ be a connected compact smooth oriented embedded surface with boundary $K$, oriented so that its boundary orientation is the given orientation of $K$. Let $g$ be the nonnegative integer determined by $\chi(F)=1-2g$. Choose an ordered integral basis $a_1,\ldots,a_{2g}$ of the first singular homology group $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)$, represented by integral one-cycles on $F$. Orient the normal line of $F$ by requiring $(n,u,v)$ to be positively oriented in $S^3$ whenever $(u,v)$ is a positive tangent basis of $F$. The positive push-off $a_i^+$ is the cycle carried to a sufficiently small positive normal level in a bicollar of $F$.

For disjoint oriented closed curves $J,L\subset S^3$, orient a meridian $\mu_L$ of $L$ so that a positive tangent to $L$ followed by a positive basis of its normal disk gives the ambient orientation. The linking number $\operatorname{lk}(J,L)$ is the integer determined by $[J]=\operatorname{lk}(J,L)[\mu_L]$ in $H_1(S^3\setminus L;\mathbb Z)$, using the Alexander-duality identification that sends $[\mu_L]$ to $1$. Extend linking additively over integral one-cycles. The Seifert pairing is $\theta_F(x,y)=\operatorname{lk}(x^+,y)$, and its matrix in the chosen basis is $V=(V_{ij})_{i,j=1}^{2g}$, where $V_{ij}=\theta_F(a_i,a_j)=\operatorname{lk}(a_i^+,a_j)$. The surface and basis are part of the data; this definition asserts no knot-only matrix invariant.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented embedded circle in the oriented standard three-sphere, let $F$ be a connected compact smooth oriented embedded surface with boundary $K$, and let $a_1,\ldots,a_{2g}$ be the ordered integral basis and positive normal push-off convention used to define the Seifert matrix $V$ above. Every class of $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)$ has a representative that is a finite integral sum of pairwise disjoint smooth oriented embedded circles in $F$. For such representatives $x$ and $y$, the sum of the pairwise linking numbers between the positive push-off of $x$ and $y$ depends only on $[x]$ and $[y]$, is independent of the sufficiently small positive push-off, and equals the bilinear extension of $V_{ij}=\operatorname{lk}(a_i^+,a_j)$. The linking number of two disjoint oriented circle components is symmetric. In particular, the Seifert pairing is a well-defined bilinear map $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)\times H_1(F;\mathbb Z)\to\mathbb Z$.

Assume AC. Let $M$ be a compact $R$-oriented $n$-manifold with boundary $A$, for a commutative unital ring $R$. Cap with its relative fundamental class gives isomorphisms, for every integer $p$,
$$S_p:H^p(M;R)\xrightarrow{\sim}H_{n-p}(M,A;R),\qquad T_p:H^p(M,A;R)\xrightarrow{\sim}H_{n-p}(M;R).$$
Here both maps send a class $a$ to $a\cap[M,A]$ in the displayed target. Empty boundary recovers Poincaré duality. Disconnected and empty manifolds are included. AC is inherited only from the exhaustion and local universal-coefficient arguments in Poincaré duality.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be disjoint finite rational $1$-cycles in the boundary $S^3$ of the standard oriented $4$-ball $B^4$, each represented as a finite rational linear combination of oriented knots. Let $P$ and $Q$ be finite rational $2$-chains in $B^4$ with $\partial P=\alpha$ and $\partial Q=\beta$, with common standard product collars at their respective boundaries and with their interiors in general position. Then the signed interior intersection number $P\cdot Q$ equals the bilinear extension of the linking number $\operatorname{lk}(\alpha,\beta)$ defined by positive meridians in $S^3$.

Let $H$ be a free abelian group of rank $2g$ and let $V:H\times H\to\mathbb Z$ be a bilinear form. Write $H_{\mathbb Q}=H\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb Q$ and extend $V$ $\mathbb Q$-bilinearly to $H_{\mathbb Q}$. If $L\subset H_{\mathbb Q}$ is a $\mathbb Q$-subspace of dimension $g$ and $V(x,y)=0$ for all $x,y\in L$, then $M=H\cap L$ is a rank-$g$ direct summand of $H$ and $V|_{M\times M}=0$.

Assume full AC. Let $D$ be a locally flat properly embedded disk in the standard four-ball $B^4$ with boundary an oriented knot $K\subset S^3$, and let $F\subset S^3$ be a connected oriented Seifert surface for $K$. After matching product collars and pushing the interior of $F$ slightly into $B^4$, the closed locally flat surface $\Sigma=F\cup_KD$ bounds a compact connected oriented locally flat three-manifold $R\subset B^4$. The conclusion includes an oriented ambient product neighborhood of $R$ on both sides, with the positive normal push-off along the $F$ portion of $\partial R=\Sigma$ lying on the complementary side of $R$.

Assume countable choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. For every smooth manifold $M$, possibly with boundary, the inclusion of smooth into continuous real singular chains induces an isomorphism
$$H_k^\infty(M;\mathbb R)\longrightarrow H_k^{\mathrm{sing}}(M;\mathbb R)$$
in every integer degree. This isomorphism is natural for smooth maps. The proof smooths only finitely many simplices at a time. For boundary targets it moves a finite compact set into the interior; it does not prescribe arbitrary boundary faces during smoothing.

Assume full AC. Every compact topological three-manifold $M$, with boundary allowed, is homeomorphic to the realization of a finite combinatorial three-manifold triangulation, with boundary allowed (the empty complex when $M=\varnothing$). Its boundary is the realization of a subcomplex. Thus $M$ admits a finite compatible PL structure, without any previously supplied smooth or PL structure on its interior.

If a TOP product collar of the boundary, together with a finite PL structure on its boundary surface, has already been supplied, the new PL structure may be chosen equal to that product PL structure on a smaller boundary neighborhood. No smooth marking or smooth ambient isotopy is asserted. Full AC remains the hypothesis of this theorem; no choice-free theorem is obtained by omitting that premise.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented embedded circle in the oriented standard three-sphere, let $F$ be a connected compact smooth oriented embedded surface with boundary $K$, and let $a_1,\ldots,a_{2g}$ be any ordered integral basis of $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)$ with Seifert matrix $V_{ij}=\operatorname{lk}(a_i^+,a_j)$. Let $J_F$ be the matrix of the algebraic intersection form on $F$, with a transverse intersection of oriented curves $u,v$ counted positively exactly when their ordered tangent vectors form a positive basis of $TF$. Then $V-V^T=J_F$. The matrix $J_F$ is skew-symmetric and unimodular; when $a_1,\ldots,a_{2g}$ is a standard handle basis, it is a direct sum of blocks $\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\-1&0\end{pmatrix}$.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice-principle-for-foliation-pair]]). Let $S$ be an oriented Hausdorff $C^2$ surface without boundary, possibly disconnected. Then:

1. Every compact subset $K\subset S$ lies in the interior of a compact finitely cellulated $C^2$ subsurface $N$. If $K$ is contained in one connected component of $S$, $N$ can be chosen connected. A specified finite embedded regular $C^2$ graph contained in $\operatorname{Int}N$ can be included in its one-skeleton.
2. Every connected closed compact subsurface has an oriented genus normal form: the sphere for $g=0$, or the polygon word $\prod_{i=1}^g a_i b_i a_i^{-1}b_i^{-1}$ for $g\ge1$, with $\chi=2-2g$. A connected compact subsurface with $b>0$ boundary circles has a free fundamental group; capping its boundaries defines genus $g$ and gives $\chi=2-2g-b$ and free rank $2g+b-1$.
3. The fundamental group of every connected component of $S$ is torsion-free.
4. Every regular embedded $C^2$ nullhomotopic circle $c$ bounds an embedded compact disk region in $S$. Here a disk region is a compact subsurface homeomorphic to the closed disk, with boundary exactly $c$; its inherited surface structure and boundary are $C^2$. It is unique unless the **connected component containing $c$** is a sphere; in that component the two complementary disk regions are the two possibilities.

The normal forms in clause 2 are homeomorphism normal forms. No general differentiable smoothing theorem or arbitrary-surface triangulation-existence theorem is a premise of this item.

For $A\subseteq X$ there is an exact sequence
$$\cdots\to H_n(A;G)\to H_n(X;G)\to H_n(X,A;G)\xrightarrow{\delta}H_{n-1}(A;G)\to H_{n-1}(X;G)\to\cdots.$$

If $M$ is a compact topological manifold with boundary $A=\partial M$, there is an open neighborhood $V$ of $A$ and a homeomorphism
$$c:A\times[0,1)\xrightarrow{\sim}V,\qquad c(x,0)=x.$$
Consequently $A\hookrightarrow M$ is an unbased cofibration, and $M\setminus A\hookrightarrow M$ is a homotopy equivalence. The manifold is Hausdorff and second countable by convention. All three conclusions require no AC.

Let $\mathcal L$ be one local system on $X$.

1. If $Z\subseteq A\subseteq X$ and $\overline Z\subseteq\operatorname{int}_X(A)$, inclusion induces excision isomorphisms in both local homology and local cohomology between $(X\setminus Z,A\setminus Z)$ and $(X,A)$, using the restrictions of $\mathcal L$.
2. For an open cover $X=U\cup V$, there are natural exact sequences
   $$\cdots\to H_n(U\cap V;\mathcal L)\to H_n(U;\mathcal L)\oplus H_n(V;\mathcal L)\to H_n(X;\mathcal L)\to\cdots$$
   and
   $$\cdots\to H^n(X;\mathcal L)\to H^n(U;\mathcal L)\oplus H^n(V;\mathcal L)\to H^n(U\cap V;\mathcal L)\to\cdots,$$
   where all systems are restrictions and the middle difference map in cohomology is $u|_{U\cap V}-v|_{U\cap V}$.

The same conclusions hold for the standard excisive-cover condition after replacing the cover by interiors. A local system given only on a subspace is not silently assumed to extend to $X$.
For a finite CW complex, $\chi(X)=\sum_n(-1)^n\operatorname{rank}H_n(X;\mathbb Z)$.

Assume AC. Let $M$ be an $R$-oriented boundaryless $n$-manifold, with $R$ commutative unital; manifolds are Hausdorff and second countable here. Then cap with the compatible compact orientation classes gives isomorphisms
$$D_M:H_c^p(M;R)\xrightarrow{\sim}H_{n-p}(M;R)$$
for every integer $p$, including disconnected, noncompact and empty $M$.

Naturality means that for an open inclusion $i:U\hookrightarrow M$ with restricted orientation, $D_M e=i_*D_U$, where $e$ is extension of compact supports. For compact $M$, $H_c^p(M;R)=H^p(M;R)$ canonically and $D_M(a)=a\cap[M]$. For arbitrary $M$ the isomorphism is the direct sum of those on its components. AC is used in the countable coordinate-neighborhood selection for exhaustion and in the local universal-coefficient proof.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $R$ be a PID, $C$ a chain complex of free
$R$-modules, and $G$ an $R$-module. Then naturally
$$0\to\operatorname{Ext}^1_R(H_{n-1}C,G)\to H^n\operatorname{Hom}_R(C,G)\xrightarrow{\operatorname{ev}_n}\operatorname{Hom}_R(H_nC,G)\to0$$
is exact.

derivations.claim: Construct the compact oriented locally flat $R$ by [F5], and write $\Sigma=\partial R=F\cup D$ after matching collars. The Axiom of Choice [A1] is the hypothesis under which the supplied Seifert-pairing and duality interfaces are invoked. Capping the sole boundary circle of $F$ by a disk does not change $H_1$ because that circle is already the boundary of the oriented fundamental $2$-chain of $F$; by [F9] and exactness [F10], $H_1(F;\mathbb Q)\cong H_1(\Sigma;\mathbb Q)$ has dimension $2g$. In the pair sequence [F10], $H_0(\Sigma;\mathbb Q)\to H_0(R;\mathbb Q)$ is an isomorphism because both are connected. Exactness therefore makes $H_1(R;\mathbb Q)\to H_1(R,\Sigma;\mathbb Q)$ surjective. By [F2] and [F14], the target has dimension $b_2(R)$, so the image of $H_1(\Sigma;\mathbb Q)\to H_1(R;\mathbb Q)$ has dimension $b_1(R)-b_2(R)$.

Let $\widehat R$ be the double of $R$ along $\Sigma$, with the second copy oppositely oriented so the orientations glue. Its two copies have open collar thickenings with intersection retracting to $\Sigma$, so [F11] gives $\chi(\widehat R)=2\chi(R)-\chi(\Sigma)$. By [F12] and [F13], $\chi(\widehat R)=0$, and by [F9], $\chi(\Sigma)=2-2g$; hence $\chi(R)=1-g$. Also [F2] gives $H_3(R;\mathbb Q)\cong H^0(R,\Sigma;\mathbb Q)=0$: a relative zero-cocycle is locally constant on the connected $R$ and vanishes on the nonempty connected $\Sigma$, so it is zero. With $b_0(R)=1$, the rational Euler-characteristic identity [F13] implies $b_1(R)-b_2(R)=g$. Thus the kernel $L=\ker(H_1(\Sigma;\mathbb Q)\to H_1(R;\mathbb Q))$, identified with a subspace of $H_1(F;\mathbb Q)$, has dimension $2g-g=g$.

Represent $x,y\in L$ by finite rational smooth cycles in the given $F$, away from $K$, and choose finite rational continuous bounding chains in $R$. Use its pre-collar-push model and the actual positive normal product of [F5]. Push the first chain into the positive complementary side, with boundary the actual positive Seifert push $x^+$; leave the second chain in $R$ with boundary $y$. An intrinsic boundary-collar push of their interiors and the common product near $F$ give the usual collared bounding chains in $B^4$, missing the corner $K$. Their supports are disjoint compact sets by the actual two-sided product. Choose disjoint relatively open smooth ambient neighborhoods $U,V\subset B^4$ of those supports, including their boundary cycles; these are smooth manifolds with boundary as open subsets of the standard smooth ball. In $U$, [F6] makes the smooth cycle $x^+$ bound a finite smooth real chain, since it bounds continuously there; likewise $y$ bounds in $V$. In each finite set of occurring simplices the equations for the boundary coefficients are rational, so rational Gaussian elimination replaces the real coefficients by rational ones without enlarging support. Near $S^3$, move the interiors inward and attach the standard product of the fixed boundary cycle with the collar interval. This puts both chains in common standard end collars, still in disjoint $U,V$. They therefore have empty interior intersection, and [F3] gives $V_{\mathbb Q}(x,y)=\operatorname{lk}(x^+,y)=0$. The smoothing here concerns only chains in the disjoint smooth ambient regions; it assumes no smooth structure on $R$ or its TOP normal chart.

Apply the integral-saturation result [F4] to this $g$-dimensional rational isotropic subspace: $M=H_1(F;\mathbb Z)\cap L$ is a primitive rank-$g$ direct summand with $V|_{M\times M}=0$. By [F8] the pairing is on an integral Seifert lattice, so the metabolic-form definition makes $M$ a metabolizer. This proves the Statement for every locally flat slice disk, including every smooth slice disk.

axioms.label: A1
axioms.statement: Full AC is the family-of-nonempty-sets choice axiom used by the Seifert-pairing convention. [[def-axiom-of-choice]]

risk_review.notes: Independently checked every current proof step and all F1–F14 supplier statements. Confirmed refuter74:1: old3.1 applied smooth-chain homology inside merely locally flat R, despite F6 disclaimer. Removed that redundant subproof and applied the existing general argument to all disks. Pair exactness and rational duality give image rank b1-b2; doubling and finite TOP triangulation give chi(R)=1-g and b3=0, hence kernel rank g, including g=0. Continuous rational chains push apart in the actual positive normal product; only their disjoint open subsets of the standard smooth ball are smoothed. Finite rational boundary equations replace real coefficients by rational ones; collars stay in those disjoint neighborhoods. Linking/intersection is therefore zero and saturation gives a primitive rank-half summand. No smooth structure on the embedded R is asserted. Statement and dependencies unchanged; repaired proof includes smooth disks.
